title: "Resources"
order: 94
---

Nine places to check this module's reasoning yourself, or go deeper on the definitions it
leans on. All were checked and loading (via `curl`) at the time this page was written.

- **[45 CFR 160.103, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-160/subpart-A/section-160.103)**
  — the current, official text of the section this entire module is built on: covered entity,
  health care provider, business associate, protected health information, and individually
  identifiable health information, all in one place. This is the primary source `sources/cfr/45-160.103.md`
  was excerpted from — read the full section if you want the definitions this module didn't need
  (health plan, health care clearinghouse, and the health-plan sub-definitions among them).

- **[45 CFR 160.102, eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-160/subpart-A/section-160.102)**
  — the applicability section sitting right next to 160.103. It states which parts of the HIPAA
  Administrative Simplification regulations apply "to the following entities," i.e., it's the
  provision that actually puts weight behind the "covered entity" label once a determination
  like this module's is made. Worth reading once alongside 160.103, not quoted here.

- **[45 CFR 160.103, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/160.103)**
  — a secondary, independently maintained mirror of the same section, useful for a fast
  cross-check or a plain-text copy to search, the same way this curriculum has used Cornell's
  mirrors for CFR sections since `csv-and-becs`.

- **[Risk Management Under the HIPAA Security Rule](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kDyrj-fJzhw)**
  (USGovHHSOCR, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson, from HHS's
  Office for Civil Rights, the HIPAA enforcement agency. Covers the Security Rule's risk
  management requirement for covered entities; it is not about covered-entity status or blood
  centers, so read it as a preview of what covered-entity status obligates, not as an answer to
  this lesson's question. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[CMS: Covered Entity? (includes the Covered Entity Decision Tool)](https://www.cms.gov/priorities/key-initiatives/burden-reduction/administrative-simplification/hipaa/covered-entities)**
  — the federal agency's own page for "Not sure if you're a covered entity?", with a decision
  tool. This is the closest official counterpart to the reasoning this lesson does by hand from
  160.103; use it when someone asks how an organization would actually check its own status.
  Verified loading via  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 162.923, Requirements for covered entities (Cornell LII)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/162.923)**
  — the section of the transaction-standards rules that states what covered entities must do when
  conducting a covered transaction electronically. This lesson says "covered transaction" lives
  outside 160.103; this is one place to start reading that side. Not quoted in the lesson.
  Verified loading via  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.530, Administrative requirements (Cornell LII)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.530)**
  — among other things, requires a covered entity to designate a privacy official and a contact
  person for complaints, and to train its workforce. Read it for the Privacy Rule's governance
  roles, which this lesson does not teach. Verified loading via  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[45 CFR 164.308, Administrative safeguards (eCFR)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.308)**
  — includes the "assigned security responsibility" standard: a covered entity must identify the
  security official responsible for its Security Rule policies and procedures. The Security Rule
  counterpart to the privacy official above; taught in full in `security-rule-safeguards-and-part-11`.
  Verified loading via  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-66 Rev. 2: Implementing the HIPAA Security Rule — A Cybersecurity Resource Guide](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/66/r2/final)**
  — NIST's practical guide for putting the Security Rule into practice, for readers who want to
  see how a covered entity organizes security work beyond what the rule's text says. Verified
  loading via  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
